item.title: Investigators release information from flight data recorder in Miami plane crash
item.description: Safety investigators are releasing new details about the moments before the deadly cargo plane crash in Miami on Sunday, raising questions about the actions of the two pilots.

item.title: Conductor Julian Wachner receives suspended sentence for possession of child sex abuse material
item.description: The formerly prominent, widely recorded conductor was sentenced Wednesday to nearly six years of probation for five counts of possession of child sex abuse material in Indianapolis.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
item.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.

item.title: Andrew Tate is denied bail and will remain in jail during his extradition fight
item.description: Prosecutors told the court that Andrew and Tristan Tate boasted about having multiple passports and flying on private jets. But the Tates' lawyers argued they were only playing a role for their fans.

item.title: Cargo jet tried to abort unsteady landing before Miami crash, flight data indicates
item.description: Flight data suggest an Amazon cargo plane tried to abort an unsteady landing at Miami International Airport before smashing into a van and killing five people inside, according to information investigators released Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: National Guard member arrested after drawing gun on fellow soldier in D.C.
item.description: A member of the Georgia National Guard deployed in Washington, D.C., as part of a task force to fight crime, has been arrested for pulling a gun on a fellow Guard member in an alleged dispute over regulation haircuts.

item.title: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
item.description: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.

item.title: Ballot seizures seemed impossible. But judges and officials are prepping for them now
item.description: The idea of law enforcement taking possession of ballots in the middle of an active election used to be considered impossible. Now, it's a scenario voting officials — and judges — are training for.

item.description: Voters and election officials are navigating uncertainty about mail-in voting for the midterms as the legal fight drags on over the U.S. Postal Service plan for President Trump's bid for restrictions.

item.title: New York City Mayor Mamdani releases documents related to post-9/11 air quality
item.description: New York City has released 170,000 documents it says show officials knew the air quality around the World Trade Center after 9/11 was dangerous to breathe, but they didn't warn local residents.
